headline: A 2014 law updates the legal descriptions of two Utah water-project properties in the Provo River Project Transfer Act.
what_it_does: The law changes the definitions of two terms in the Provo River Project Transfer Act. It redefines the "Pleasant Grove Property" as a specific Utah land parcel of the Provo River Project's Deer Creek Division, as it exists when conveyed. It also redefines the "Provo Reservoir Canal" to cover the historic canal, its related structures, and land and rights-of-way, running from the Murdock Diversion Dam to the point where water is discharged into two named canals, again as it exists at the time of conveyance.

who_it_affects.group: Water users and irrigation districts served by the Provo River Project canal system
who_it_affects.how: The law clarifies which physical facilities and parcels are covered when they are transferred under the Act, which may affect who manages or owns them.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Utah's Provo and Utah County area
who_it_affects.how: Because the canal and land described are in this region, local communities may see changes in how these facilities are handled after transfer.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on July 25, 2014, though the redefined properties apply when they are actually conveyed under the Act.
